info.title: daylight_server
info.summary: GPU annual daylight and solar simulation on meshes, over HTTP.
info.description:
Runs the [kit-sim_daylight](https://github.com/Cybernaut0815/kit-sim_daylight) core (OptiX ray tracing, Radiance-derived Perez sky, validated against Ladybug Tools, Radiance and pvlib) for several users at once. One GPU worker runs queued jobs one after another; uploads, validation, cached answers and status polls never wait for it.

## Workflow

1. **Upload each mesh once** as a `.dmesh` image: `PUT /mesh/{id}` with an id you choose (a UUID). Meshes stay cached in server RAM, so later runs only name them.
2. **Submit a job**: `POST /jobs` (multipart) with the receiving meshes in `sensors`, the shading-only meshes in `context`, CLI flags in `args`, and weather as an `epw` file, an `epw_url`, or `--clear-sky`. A `404` with `{"missing": [...]}` lists ids the server does not have: upload those and submit again.
3. **Wait**: `GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25` returns as soon as the state or the queue position changes (long poll). Repeat while `state` is `queued` or `running`.
4. **Read the result** when `state` is `done`: `values_b64` is base64 of float64 little-endian values, row-major `[rows x columns.length]`, rows = sum of `meshes[].count`. Rows of mesh *k* are `first .. first + count - 1`, one per face (or per vertex with `--on vertices`) in the uploaded order.
5. **Cancel** with `DELETE /jobs/{id}` when the result is no longer needed; the GPU moves on to the next job.

`POST /run` does steps 2 to 4 in one blocking call and answers the result object directly.

## Example

```sh
curl -T box.dmesh "http://localhost:8080/mesh/3f1c0b9e-0d59-4a8e-9a43-1b7a6a0c2e11?name=roof"
curl -F sensors=3f1c0b9e-0d59-4a8e-9a43-1b7a6a0c2e11 -F args=--lat -F args=52.52 -F args=--lon -F args=13.41 -F args=--tz -F args=1 \
     -F args=--quantity -F args=radiation,sunhours -F args=--clear-sky http://localhost:8080/jobs
curl "http://localhost:8080/jobs/<id from the answer>?wait=25"
```

Decoding in Python: `numpy.frombuffer(base64.b64decode(r['values_b64']), '<f8').reshape(-1, len(r['columns']))`. In JavaScript: `new Float64Array(Uint8Array.from(atob(r.values_b64), c => c.charCodeAt(0)).buffer)`.

## Units and conventions

Coordinates in `.dmesh` are metres, Z up, right-handed winding (the face normal points to the front side). `radiation`, `direct`, `diffuse`: kWh/m² over the evaluated period; `irradiance`: W/m² mean; `illuminance`: lux mean; `sunhours`: hours (equivalent full-sun hours with `--transmission on`). Columns are named `<quantity>_<side>` (`radiation_front`, `sunhours_back`).

Surfaces are opaque and black by default (the only reflection is the `--ground` plane beyond the model). The server takes numbers, no materials: a `.dmesh` may give each face an optics slot, `--optics` gives a mesh or a slot its reflectance and transmittance, `--transmission on` lets light through glass and porous slots, `--fresnel` picks angle-dependent or flat glass, and `--bounces N` adds the light the model reflects, up to N diffuse reflections traced with `--bounce-samples` paths per sensor (see `args`).

## Errors and limits

Errors are `text/plain`, first line `error: <cause>`; usage errors are `400` and include the CLI usage text. `--optics` rows are checked twice: grammar and ranges at submission (`400`, as are `--bounces` and `--bounce-samples` out of range and the switches ladybug mode refuses), names and slots against the run's meshes when the job runs (the job ends in `error`, status 500). `429`: this client already has `--client-jobs` (default 2) jobs queued or running; identify a client with the `X-Client-Id` header (else the network address). `503`: the queue holds `--max-queue` (default 32) jobs. Both carry `Retry-After`. Finished jobs are kept 15 minutes. There is no authentication; job ids are random UUIDs that only their submitter knows.

## Agents (MCP)

With `--mcp`, agents on this machine (Claude Code, Claude Desktop) work with the web app over MCP: they open models, set roles and settings, run, read results, set cameras, take screenshots, edit charts and write PDF reports, and talk about what the results mean. `POST /mcp` (`mcpMessage`, tag `agents`) is their endpoint; its description covers the protocol, how to connect and the tools. The other `agents` routes serve the app itself, and all of them answer only requests from this machine.

Without `--mcp` every route here answers `404`; a request that does not come from this machine gets `403`.

put.description:
Stores one mesh in the server's RAM cache under the id you chose (least recently used meshes are evicted when the cache is full; a later job naming an evicted id gets a `404 {missing}` and you upload it again). Uploading an existing id replaces it. The body is one `.dmesh` image, little-endian, no padding:

| offset | type | content |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | char[4] | `DLM1` |
| 4 | uint32 | flags: bit 0 = a slot block follows the indices; other bits must be 0 |
| 8 | uint64 | n_points |
| 16 | uint64 | n_faces |
| 24 | uint64 | n_indices |
| 32 | float64[3 n_points] | xyz, metres, Z up |
| | int32[n_faces] | vertices per face (>= 3), right-handed winding |
| | int32[n_indices] | 0-based point indices, sum(counts) = n_indices |
| | uint16[n_faces] | only with flags bit 0: the optics slot of each face, which `--optics NAME/SLOT=...` addresses (without the block every face is slot 0) |

Another flag bit or a short slot block is a `400`. The TypeScript binding writes it with `toDmesh(mesh)` (the slot block when `ObjMesh.slots` is set), the Python binding with `daylight.to_dmesh(...)`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Display name, echoed back in result `meshes[].name` (sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, made unique per run: a second `roof` in one run, ignoring case, is `roof_2`). Defaults to the id. It is the NAME that `--optics` rows address.

get.summary: Check whether a mesh is cached
get.description: Answers 204 when the server holds the mesh, 404 when it must be uploaded (again).

post.description: Validates the request at once (bad flags, unknown mesh ids, unusable weather fail here) and queues the run for the GPU. Answers the job: `202` while queued, or `200` with a finished job when an identical request was answered before (same mesh ids, args and weather; `cache.response` is then `hit`). Follow it with `GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25`.

200.description: Answered from the result cache: the job is already `done`.

get.summary: Queue overview and this client's jobs
get.description: How busy the GPU is, and the jobs submitted by this client (same `X-Client-Id`, else the same network address). Other clients' job ids are never listed.

get.summary: Get a job, optionally waiting for a change
get.description: The job's state and queue position; when `done` it carries the result fields (`columns`, `meshes`, `values_b64`, ...), when `error` or `cancelled` the message and `status`. With `wait=S` the call returns as soon as the state or the position changes, at the latest after S seconds (long poll; poll again while `queued` or `running`).

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a change, 0 to 30.

delete.description: A queued job leaves the queue at once (`cancelled`); a running one stops at its next trace chunk (still `running` in this answer, `cancelled` shortly after). A finished job is returned unchanged.

post.description: Submits like `submitJob` and keeps the request open until the job finishes, then answers the result object directly (the same fields a `done` job carries, without the job fields). Simple for scripts; for long runs or a progress display use `submitJob` + `getJob`.

409.description: Cancelled while it ran (`DELETE /jobs/{id}` from another request).

text/plain.example: error: cancelled

500.description: The simulation failed (runtime error from the core), also when an `--optics` row does not resolve against the run's meshes (a NAME no mesh has, or several have; a slot the mesh does not have; a row given twice).

get.summary: Download a weather resource through the server cache
get.description:
Fetches one of a fixed set of public weather resources once and serves it from disk afterwards (browsers cannot fetch them directly: no CORS). The same URLs work as `epw_url` in a run. Allowed prefixes:

- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NREL/EnergyPlus/develop/weather/master.geojson`: the EnergyPlus weather station index (GeoJSON; each feature's `properties.epw` is an HTML anchor whose `href` is the station's EPW)
- `https://energyplus-weather.s3.amazonaws.com/`: EnergyPlus weather files (EPW)
- `https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/v5_3/tmy?`: PVGIS typical meteorological year, e.g. `...tmy?lat=52.52&lon=13.41&outputformat=epw` (modelled, any location, 30 requests per second per IP)

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The resource URL, URL-encoded (its own `&` must not split the query).

text/plain.example:
LOCATION,unknown,-,unknown,ECMWF/ERA,unknown,52.520000,13.410000,1,47
...
error: url not in the allowlist

post.description:
The web app's MCP server for agents on this machine, such as Claude Code and Claude Desktop. It answers the handshake and the tool list itself and relays each tool call to the app open in a browser tab (`bridgeNext`), which carries it out with everything its UI offers and shows it live: models, roles, settings, runs, results, cameras, screenshots, charts and reports. With no app tab open, the server starts the app hidden in headless Chrome (with `--web` or `--app-url`) and the agent works there; opening the app later picks that session up.

## Protocol

MCP Streamable HTTP, the revisions with the `initialize` handshake: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26. One JSON-RPC message per POST, answered as `application/json`: no SSE stream (`mcpGet` answers 405), no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no batches, no prompts or resources.

| message | answer |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | `protocolVersion` (the one asked for when supported, else `2025-11-25`), `capabilities: {tools: {}}`, `serverInfo`, `instructions` (how to work with the app) |
| `ping` | `{}` |
| `tools/list` | every tool, in one page |
| `tools/call` | the app's `CallToolResult` (`arguments` may be left out) |
| a notification (no `id`) | `202`, no body; `notifications/cancelled` too: hanging up cancels a call |
| anything else (`prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `server/discover`, ...) | error `-32601` |

JSON-RPC errors come with HTTP 200 and echo the request's `id` as sent; a `tools/call` of a tool `tools/list` does not name gets `-32602` (`Unknown tool`). A body that is not one JSON object gets `400` with `-32700` (`-32600` for a batch, a body without a `method`, or an `id` that is not a string or a number). A request other than `initialize` whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header names another revision gets `400 text/plain`, so a client probing for 2026-07-28 falls back to `initialize`.

**Every call answers within 55 s** (Claude Desktop ends tool calls at about 60 s, and Claude Code waits 60 s for an HTTP answer by default). Long steps (a run, a big model, a PDF) go on in the app and the reply says `running` or `generating`: call the tool again. What the agent can act on comes back as an `isError` result: no app tab open (ask the user to open the app and keep its tab open), or no answer within 55 s (the step may still be running in the app: call `app_state`).

## Connect

Start `daylight_server --web ..\web\dist --mcp` (`--web` serves the app at http://localhost:8080/ and lets the server start the hidden instance), then:

- **Claude Code** (HTTP): `claude mcp add --transport http daylight http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp`; `/mcp` in Claude Code lists the tools. If it does not connect, start Claude Code with the environment variable `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy` (no probe for 2026-07-28).
- **Claude Desktop** (stdio only: its connectors run in Anthropic's cloud and cannot reach this machine): merge the entry below into `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` with absolute paths (`where node` shows node.exe) and restart Claude Desktop. `server/mcp-stdio.mjs` (Node 18 or later, no packages) relays each message to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp`; a URL after the script path picks another address.

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "daylight": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe", "args": ["F:\\Github\\kit-sim_daylight_frontend\\server\\mcp-stdio.mjs"] } } }
```

## Tools

Models by letter A-D, building parts by USD prim path, times in local standard time; `tools/list` gives each tool's description and input schema.

- **App and knowledge:** `app_state` (call it first), `guide` (`daylight`, `report`, `kit-ui`), `site_info`
- **Models and inputs:** `open_model`, `remove_model`, `model_tree`, `set_roles` (receiver, shade, none), `set_visibility`, `set_geometry`, `get_materials`, `edit_material`, `update_settings` (site, time, simulation, weather, colour scales, charts)
- **Runs and results:** `run`, `results`, `find_critical`, `download_result`
- **Views and images:** `set_display`, `set_camera`, `save_view`, `screenshot` (any width and height; never moves the user's camera)
- **Reports:** `get_report`, `save_report`, `delete_report`, `generate_report` (one option, or 2 to 4 compared; a PDF in the kit-ui kit-report layout whose charts and cameras the user can edit in the app)

parameters.name: MCP-Protocol-Version
parameters.description: The revision agreed in `initialize`, which clients send on every later request.

200.description: The JSON-RPC answer: the method's `result`, or an `error` (`-32601` unknown method, `-32602` a `tools/call` without a tool name or of an unknown tool). A tool that could not do its step answers a result with `isError: true` and a text saying what to do.

result.instructions: This server drives the Daylight app (sun, sky and daylight simulation on 3D building models) in the user's browser tab, ... Start with app_state. ...

content.text: No daylight app tab is open on this machine: ask the user to open the app and keep its tab open (LAN tabs cannot be driven), or to start daylight_server with --web or --app-url so it can start a hidden instance itself.

202.description: A notification (no `id`, e.g. `notifications/initialized`): accepted, no body.

400.description: Not a message this server takes: an `MCP-Protocol-Version` header naming another revision on a request other than `initialize` (a newer client then falls back to `initialize`; `text/plain`), or a body that is not one JSON object (`-32700`), a batch, a body without a `method`, or an `id` that is not a string or a number (`-32600`).

text/plain.example: error: MCP-Protocol-Version 2026-07-28 is not supported (2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26)

error.message: Parse error: the body is not one JSON object
Invalid Request: one JSON-RPC message per POST, no batches

get.description: MCP lets a server offer a `GET` stream for messages to the client; this one opens none (no SSE, no sessions), so `GET /mcp` answers `405` with `Allow: POST`. Send every message with `mcpMessage`.

text/plain.example: error: POST JSON-RPC messages to /mcp; this server opens no SSE stream

get.summary: Next tool call for an app tab (long poll)
get.description: The web app's side of the relay; agents do not call it. Each page load keeps one `wait=25` poll open and gets the next `tools/call` meant for it, its params as the agent sent them; the tab carries it out and answers with `bridgeResult`. `wait=0` is a ping that never hands out a call: it keeps the tab live and, with `focus=1`, marks it as the one the user looked at last. A call goes to a live tab (a poll open, or one seen within 5 s): the user's tabs before the hidden instance (`kind=headless`), then the one focused last, then the one seen last. With none, a tab gets 5 s to come back (a page reloading; an app retrying after a server restart, every 3 s), then the server starts the hidden instance (`--web` or `--app-url`) and gives it up to 30 s to poll; one that has not polled for a minute (its page crashed, or never reached this route) is started again. A poll from a user's tab ends a hidden instance that has no session to hand over and no call on its way. Tabs gone for a minute are forgotten.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a call, 0 to 25; 0 is a ping.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.description: `1` when the page's window has focus.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `headless` from the hidden instance; the user's tabs leave it out.

200.description: A call for this tab: its id and the `tools/call` params, raw (`arguments` added as `{}` when the agent left it out).

204.description: No call within `wait` seconds, or a ping.

get.summary: Read a model file or folder on this machine (app tab)
get.description: How the app opens a model by path (the `open_model` tool): a file's bytes, or a folder's model files, listed recursively for the tab to fetch one after another. Absolute drive-letter paths only (`C:\...` or `C:/...`; no network share, no device path) and only the Model panel's file types plus weather files: `.usd .usda .usdc .usdz .glb .gltf .obj .mtl .bin .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .exr .hdr .epw`. A file is checked as the file it opens (a symlink by its target, an 8.3 short name by its long name) and is at most `--max-mb`. A folder listing skips other files, names starting with a dot, `__MACOSX`, file symlinks and linked folders, and holds at most 2000 files and `--max-mb` in all.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path of a file or folder, URL-encoded.

200.description: A file's bytes, or a folder's listing (paths relative to the folder, `/`-separated).

400.description: Not an absolute local path, not a model, texture or weather file, or over the limits.

get.description: The reports the app stored with `saveReport`, each with its spec as a JSON string (the app parses each one by itself, so a damaged file cannot break the list) and whether a PDF exists. Each lives in `<cache>/reports/<id>/` (`--cache`, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\daylight_server`): `report.json` (the spec), `index.html` (the page last printed) and `report.pdf`. Agents reach them with the `get_report`, `save_report`, `delete_report` and `generate_report` tools.

put.description: Creates or replaces the report's `report.json` with the body: one JSON object of at most 1 MB, the app's ReportSpec (title, models, stats, summary, blocks of text, charts, views and tables), which the app validates; the server stores it as it comes. Written to a temporary file and renamed, so a crash never leaves half a spec.

example.summary: On 21 March the south facade gets 0.754 h of sun on average.

blocks.text: The neighbour to the south shades it from 10:00.

post.summary: Print a report page to PDF (app)
post.description: Saves the body, the report page the app rendered from the spec (self-contained HTML in the kit-ui kit-report layout: CSS, fonts and images inline), as `index.html` behind a Content-Security-Policy that lets it load nothing but inline styles and `data:` images and fonts (no scripts, frames or files), and prints it to `report.pdf` with headless Chrome or Edge (`--browser PATH`, else the one registered under Windows App Paths; its own profile in `<cache>/pdf-profile`), one print at a time, within 30 s. Answers the PDF's path, a URL that opens it (`getReportPdf`), its pages and bytes, and the fonts it embeds: `fallback` lists any that are not kit-ui's (Geist, Geist Mono, Space Mono, Tektur), i.e. characters those fonts lack that the browser drew with a system font (keep report text to Latin letters, digits and common punctuation).

text/html.example:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-kit="sim" data-theme="light" data-density="compact">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>/* kit-ui.css, its fonts as data URIs */</style></head>
<body><main class="report stack" id="main">...</main></body></html>

get.description: Claude-only mode: with no app tab open, the server runs the app hidden in headless Chrome (`--web` or `--app-url`; its profile in `<cache>/agent-profile`) and the agent works there. That instance records here, in memory, its settings (`settings`; `epw`: a weather file it opened by path), its subdivision level (`subdiv`), the state-changing tool calls it made (`steps`) and whether it ran (`ran`). An app tab opening later reads the record, replays it (same models, roles, settings, camera and results) and deletes it (`deleteSession`), which ends the hidden instance.

200.description: The record, as the hidden instance stored it.

204.description: No session: no hidden instance, or picked up already (not an error, so an app tab's console stays clean).

text/plain.example: error: agent routes are off (start daylight_server with --mcp)

MeshId.name: id

ClientId.name: X-Client-Id

ReportId.name: id
ReportId.description: Report id chosen by the app: 1 to 64 of `[a-z0-9-]` (lowercase: report folders ignore case on Windows).

RunRequest.description: One run: meshes by id, CLI flags, weather.

error: unknown flag --nope
usage: daylight <mesh>... [flags]
...

error: the queue is full (32 jobs); retry shortly

sensors.description: Ids of the receiving meshes (analysed; they also cast shade unless `--no-self-occlude`). Rows of the result follow this order.

context.description: Ids of meshes that only cast shade.

args.description:
Flags of the `daylight` CLI, one array element per token (`["--quantity", "radiation,sunhours"]`).

| flag | value | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--quantity` | `Q[,Q...]` | `radiation` | one column per quantity: `radiation` kWh/m² over the period, `direct` (sun only: beam x transmittance), `diffuse` (sky + ground, x transmittance; with `--bounces` also the light the model reflects, its reflected sun included), `irradiance` mean W/m², `illuminance` mean lux (physical mode), `sunhours` equivalent full-sun hours (an hour behind a surface transmitting 0.6 counts 0.6; with every surface opaque, the default, an exact count of sunlit hours). Transmittance is 1 for open sky and 0 behind an opaque surface; between only with `--transmission on`. With `--bounces` above 0, radiation, diffuse, irradiance and illuminance include the light reflected by the model; direct and sun hours never do |
| `--on` | `faces` / `vertices` | `faces` | one row per face (sensor at the centroid) or per point |
| `--sides` | `front` / `back` / `both` | `front` | receiving hemisphere; `both` gives two columns per quantity |
| `--mode` | `physical` / `ladybug` | `physical` | sky and sun model; `ladybug` reproduces Ladybug Tools RadiationStudy (every surface opaque and black: `--transmission on` and `--bounces` above 0 are refused, `--optics` does nothing) |
| `--lat` `--lon` | degrees, N and E positive | from the EPW | site; required without weather |
| `--tz` | hours, E positive | EPW header, else round(lon / 15) | the clock of `--time`, `--from`, `--to`, `--hours`: standard time, no DST. An EPW keeps its own zone and these times are moved into it, so each hour of weather stays with its own sun |
| `--clear-sky` | flag | off | synthesise a cloudless year (Ineichen-Perez) instead of an EPW |
| `--turbidity` | Linke turbidity | `3` | atmosphere for `--clear-sky` |
| `--altitude` | metres | `0` | site elevation for `--clear-sky` |
| `--time` | `[YYYY-]MM-DDTHH:MM` | annual | one instant; DNI/DHI interpolated between the hours around it |
| `--from` `--to` | timestamps | annual | the range `[from, to)`, the sun at the middle of each step |
| `--step` | minutes | `60` | step of `--from/--to`; DNI/DHI interpolated between the hour centres |
| `--hours` | `HH:MM-HH:MM` | whole day | with `--from/--to`: only these hours of every day (an analysis period, e.g. 09:00-17:00 from 1 Jun to 31 Aug) |
| `--sky-density` | `1` / `2` / `4` | `1` | 145 / 577 / 2305 sky patches |
| `--patch-samples` | square number | `1` | stratified rays per sky patch (physical mode) |
| `--ground` | 0..1 | `0.2` | ground reflectance |
| `--optics` | `SPEC[;SPEC...]`, SPEC = `NAME[/SLOT]=RHO[,TAU[,KIND]]`, repeatable | every slot RHO 0.2, TAU 0 | numbers per mesh or face slot (the `.dmesh` slot block, see `uploadMesh`): RHO diffuse reflectance, TAU transmittance at normal incidence, each 0..1, RHO + TAU <= 1. KIND `porous` (TAU at every angle: screens, trees; the default when TAU > 0) or `glass` (Radiance glass, n 1.52: RHO 0, 0 < TAU <= 0.918; 0.64 = double low-e). NAME = the mesh's `name` from `uploadMesh` (its id by default), `*` = every mesh; `/SLOT` = a trailing `/` and digits (`roof/1` = slot 1 of `roof`); `;` packs several SPECs into one token. Precedence NAME/SLOT > NAME > `*` > built-in. Grammar and ranges are checked at submission (`400`); a NAME no mesh of the run has (or several have), a slot the mesh does not have, or a row given twice fail the job when it runs (`error`, status 500). No effect by itself: TAU needs `--transmission on`, RHO needs `--bounces` (without it every surface is black) |
| `--transmission` | `off` / `on` | `off` | `on` (physical mode only, `400` with `--mode ladybug`): light passes glass and porous slots, weighted by their transmittance at each crossing (a closed thin solid, e.g. a pane modelled as a 1 cm box, counts once, and so does a double-faced sheet, every face repeated with the opposite winding). Free without a translucent slot (TAU > 0 on faces that cast shade); with one, rays continue through it and visibility takes 8x the memory: slower. `off`: every surface opaque, as before |
| `--fresnel` | `on` / `off` | `on` | glass transmittance by angle (Radiance `glass`: 0.64 at normal incidence passes 0.54 at 60°, 0.12 at 85°), and with `--bounces` its mirror reflectance by angle; `off`: glass passes TAU at every angle and mirrors nothing |
| `--bounces` | `0`..`20` | `0` | reflected light (physical mode only, `400` above 0 with `--mode ladybug`): what reaches a sensor after up to N diffuse reflections off the model, each by its slot's RHO. Glass mirrors its angle-dependent reflectance (`--fresnel on`; not counted in N); translucent slots pass light with `--transmission on`, otherwise every slot is opaque and glass mirrors and absorbs the rest. Paths are binned where they escape, into the sky patches (the sun binned into them, as `gendaymtx` does) or the virtual ground (`--ground`), as `rcontrib -ab N+1` daylight coefficients. 1 is the common outdoor setting (Honeybee's exterior studies use `-ab 2`), interiors need 5-8. A ground mesh hides the virtual ground from the rays it stops: without bounces they see a black surface, with them its RHO reflects the sky and sun it receives. Cost: a second pass after the visibility, linear in `--bounce-samples`; at 1024 about 2 s per million sensors on a city-like model (RTX 2060), up to 30x that among densely overlapping geometry; each further reflection adds 5-10 % outdoors (Russian roulette from the second on), more indoors. `0`: no reflection pass (no glass mirror either), as before |
| `--bounce-samples` | `64`..`65536` | `1024` | paths per sensor for `--bounces`, stratified and deterministic (a run repeats its numbers); time grows linearly with it. Noise falls as 1 / sqrt(M): at 1024 an annual facade value (street canyon, one bounce) is within 0.5 % of the converged one at the median sensor and 2.3 % at the 95th percentile, a single `--time` instant within 2.3 % / 14 % (the sun sits in a few patches); sums over many sensors are unbiased. Raise it (4096-16384) for instants and for small differences between variants |
| `--north` | degrees ccw from +Y | `0` | model north |
| `--offset` | metres | `0` | move sensors along their normal |
| `--cull-backfaces` | flag | off | occluders block only from their front side (with `--transmission on` a closed translucent solid is then crossed once, through its front faces) |
| `--no-self-occlude` | flag | off | receiving meshes do not cast shade |

Refused over HTTP: mesh file paths, `--context FILE`, `--epw FILE` (use the `epw` part or `epw_url`), `--out`, `--timeseries`, `--dump-*`, `--bench`. Weather is needed for every quantity except `sunhours`.

epw.description: An hourly EPW weather file (8760 or 8784 rows). Give this, `epw_url` or `--clear-sky`, at most one.

epw_url.description: An allowed weather URL (see `proxyDownload`); the server downloads it once and caches it.

first.description: First row of this mesh in `values_b64`.

count.description: Rows of this mesh: its faces, or its points with `--on vertices`.

response.description: `hit`: an identical request was answered from the result cache, nothing ran.

scene.description: `reused`: this run's scene was still on the GPU, so its acceleration structure was not rebuilt; `built`: it was built for this run, and is then kept like any other (`--gpu-scenes`). A scene is the job's `sensors` ids and then its `context` ids, each in their order, its `--no-self-occlude`, and the layout of the slots that cast shade: the set of those that transmit (TAU > 0 with `--transmission on`), else, with `--bounces` above 0 and a quantity other than `direct` / `sunhours`, whether their RHO or glass differ (with `--fresnel off` none is glass; either gives the scene a hit record per slot, about 20 % more acceleration-structure (GAS) memory). New `--optics` values and `--fresnel` reuse a scene as long as that layout stays; a slot that starts or stops transmitting (a TAU going from 0 to above 0 or back, or `--transmission` itself on a model with translucent slots), or `--bounces` switched on or off (with such a quantity) for a model whose slots differ in RHO or glass while none transmits, is another scene.

weather.description: `hit`: the parsed weather was cached; `none`: no weather file (clear sky or sun hours).

RunResult.description: A finished run: the CLI's output manifest, the values, and the server's timings and cache report.

ResultFields.description: The result fields; all present on a `RunResult` and on a `done` job.

columns.description: Column names `<quantity>_<side>`, in `--quantity` order, sides inner.

duration_h.description: Hours represented by the evaluated steps.

meshes.description: Receiving meshes in `sensors` order with their row ranges.

run_s.description: Seconds the GPU worker spent on this run.

total_s.description: Seconds from submission to the result (queue wait included).

JobState.description: `queued` waits for the GPU, `running` is on it; the other three are final.

position.description: Jobs ahead of this one, the running job included; 0 while running or finished.

status.description: `error`: the HTTP status `runSync` would answer (500 runtime, also an `--optics` row the run's meshes do not resolve); `cancelled`: 409.

Job.description: A job; when `state` is `done` it also carries every `RunResult` field.

jobs_retained.description: Jobs in memory, finished ones included.

agents.description: Whether this request may use the agent routes (`--mcp`, and it comes from this machine): the web app starts its side of them only then.

JsonRpcRequest.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 request, or a notification (no `id`).

id.description: Echoed in the answer exactly as sent.

JsonRpcResponse.description: The answer to one request: its `result`, or an `error`.

id.description: The request's `id`; `null` when the request could not be read.

CallToolResult.description: An MCP tool result as the app answers it: text (compact JSON or a message; a URL such as a report PDF's comes inside it) and images (JPEG, base64); `isError` when the step could not be done, its text saying what to fix.

spec.description: `report.json` as stored, as a string: parse it.

pdf.description: Absolute path of `report.pdf` on this machine.

url.description: Where `getReportPdf` serves it, on the address the request came to.

fonts.description: PostScript names of the embedded fonts, subset tags dropped.

fallback.description: The fonts that are not kit-ui's (Geist, Geist Mono, Space Mono, Tektur): the browser drew some characters with a system font. Empty for a clean report.
